characters.name: George Edward Lopez
characters.description: Abusive Parents: A big part of his backstory was how horribly irresponsible and negligent Benny was to him as a mom.His dad wasn't much better. Benevolent Boss: George went from working on the factory line to being Manager, so his fellow employees know him and respect him. In turn, George offers the same and will defend his employees when it's needed.One such case is Hosni, a Middle-Eastern employee who was being racially profiled out of a job. Had logistics been in his favor, George wouldn't have had to move him (if they had lost the contract, 20 employees would have lost their jobs, so George couldn't save Hosni from job transfer, but he made sure he got same pay).When a new GM wanted to cut a lot of employees, George managed to convince everyone to take a pay cut in order to avoid that, and even gave up a new job offer from the new owner to save everyone. Needless to say, George speaks for his employees out of respect.Benny and Ernie are zigzagged examples; he does his best to help them if they have issues at work, but they're also his mom and best friend respectively. One such case is Hosni, a Middle-Eastern employee who was being racially profiled out of a job. Had logistics been in his favor, George wouldn't have had to move him (if they had lost the contract, 20 employees would have lost their jobs, so George couldn't save Hosni from job transfer, but he made sure he got same pay). When a new GM wanted to cut a lot of employees, George managed to convince everyone to take a pay cut in order to avoid that, and even gave up a new job offer from the new owner to save everyone. Needless to say, George speaks for his employees out of respect. Benny and Ernie are zigzagged examples; he does his best to help them if they have issues at work, but they're also his mom and best friend respectively.

characters.name: Angie Palmero-Lopez
characters.description: Academic Alpha Bitch: Was a Cheerleader that initially went out with George as a joke (and then fell for him) and she won a lot of academic awards and certificates in school. A-Cup Angst: Her 34B bust size is a very sore spot for her. Berserk Button:Doesn't like it when people she helps out stabs her in the back, as shown with Marisol.Don't imply she's gonna be a "nana" (i.e., a grandmother); she is nowhere near mentally prepared for it.Hurt her kids - physically or emotionally - and she'll, in her own words, go "medieval" on you. Doesn't like it when people she helps out stabs her in the back, as shown with Marisol. Don't imply she's gonna be a "nana" (i.e., a grandmother); she is nowhere near mentally prepared for it.

characters.name: Benita "Benny" Diaz Lopez
characters.description: Abusive Parents: On both the giving and receiving ends, having been this to George when he was growing up and suffering it from her own parents. Ironically, it turns out her parents wereeven worseto her than she was to George and she was actually a better parent to her son by comparison. In one episode she slaps Max for talking back to her, and later when apologizing admits that that was how you disciplined children in her time, obviously remembering her own poor upbringing. The Alcoholic: Stated to be this and is occasionally shown drinking a beer on-screen. Ambiguously Human: Used as aRunning Gagat her expense. People question if she's even human due to her physique. Animal Motif: Is often called a "bat" by George. Berserk Button: Do NOT call her a whore, even if she said she wasn't dating boys at 15 so much as having sex with them. Later episodes would imply it's a mix of aTrauma ButtonandHeroic Self-Deprecation, having earned her already-abusive parent's everlasting resentment by getting pregnant in high school and knowing she wasn't the best parent because of it.

characters.name: Carmen Consuelo Lopez
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Why she falls for Zack, because she imagines him as a nice boy deep down who cares about her problems.In reality, he's a sleazy bastard who uses Carmen's self-esteem issues against her, bullies her into running away with him to San Francisco, plans to get her soused in order to screw her, and ditches her in San Francisco when she refuses his advances. Bratty Teenage Daughter: She wasn't initially, but she eventually degenerated into this. Buxom Beauty Standard: Masiela Lusha's breasts grew significantly larger between the first and second seasons and a plot point for one episode was George freaking out over the fact that his daughter is growing up and starting to attract attention from the boys. Cloud Cuckoolander: When she tries to be poetic and deep, her poems just sound overly dramatic and theatrical. Daddy's Girl: Subverted. George, like many fathers, is extremely protective of his "little girl". There are times when they really can't stand each other, but when push comes to shove they really do love each other. When they have a sweet moment, it is really genuine.

characters.name: Maximilian Victor Roberto Magic Johnson "Max" Lopez
characters.description: Bully Magnet: This is invoked by George and Carmen in one episode when they try to deal with Max constantly being beaten up at school. George believes it's because Angie teaches him that "bullies are friends who don't know how special you are", which George justifiably believes is guaranteed to get one's ass kicked if spoken out loud. Carmen is convinced it's because Angie still buys him nerdy clothes instead of the latest trends. Cheerful Child: Before he hit puberty that is. The Cutie: During the first two seasons. Depending on the Writer: He differs on a scale ofcloudcuckoolanderto surprisingly clever depending on the episode. Did You Think I Can't Feel?: He takes George's comments about his stupidity to heart.

characters.name: Ernesto "Ernie" Cardenas
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: Is this towards Angie from time to time. He once spent several months following her, leaving notes at her car, camping outside her home, all after she had married. George even had to threaten Ernie that his continued actions would get him arrested. Angie mentions that it was a really uncomfortable summer. Abusive Parents: Not him, as he's implied to be a productive, supportive foster father for a brief amount of time, but his parents. Ernie lives with them for most of the series and has to help take care of his morbidly obese mother, only for them to yell at him like a child. When he decides to move out and start his own life, his parents are furious and curse him for being an ungrateful, unhelpful son, proving they didn't really value him or his help despite all he did. Basement Dweller: Lived with his parents until finally moving into his own apartment in the final season. It’s shown it’s partly out of guilt and a desire to help take care of his mother, who is so morbidly obese that she can’t take care of herself. While Ernie is doing good by helping his mother, George points out her condition is not his responsibility and that nurses should be called in to help deal with such a severe situation. Big Eater: Downplayed. Despite his size he's never really shown eating much more than the other characters. Most prominently in "Ernie sees the Cellu-Light", however, he's shown to become a constant visitor to the vending machines, and is shown with a table full of food at Thirsty's. Big Handsome Man: In Season 1, a coworker is attracted to him who especially eyes his sizable rear end.

characters.name: Victor Garcia Lantigua "Vic" Palmero
characters.description: Always Someone Better: One of the few reasons George doesn't like Vic is because he had a more successful life prior to the divorce and thinks that he's a better father. Ironically, it's revealed that Vic himself came to feel this way about George, after seeing the lengths the latter went to make sure his kids grew up right - which is hammered in by how two of Vic's three kids turned out horribly while Carmen and Max remained decent, generally well-adjusted people. Ascended Extra: Started out as a recurring character in Season 2, he eventually becomes a main cast member and even moves into the Lopez family home for a time. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: A surprisingly tragic example for a sitcom; he's very bitter towards his ex-wife Emilina for cheating on him and evicting him from his home upon divorcing him, yet it's implied more than once that Vic never stoped loving Emilina as her actions continue to depress and frustrate him even several seasons later. It turns out to be mutual as, near the end of the show's run, Emilina calls Vic up saying her affair was a mistake and that she wants to reconcile; Vic is taken aback but, in the end, he elects to try and rekindle their relationship despite all the heartache Emilina put him through - and when shesuddenly dies of a heart attackright before they can do so, Vic is every bit as distraught about it as Angie. Berserk Button:Does not like to be used. He and George got into aReal Lifeversion of aFlame Warover $50 that the latter won in a poker game. He later revealed that he was lashing out because of Emilina, his wife who had cheated on him, left him and took most of his stuff.Emilina herself often becomes this after their divorce, especially in relation to her new younger lover or taking Vic's estate (which Benny often hits to get a rise out of Vic). It's later implied at points that this is because Vic never truly stopped loving Emilina, so being reminded she's with another man still stings.Don't mention Fi

characters.name: Veronica Palmero
characters.description: Advertised Extra: Since she returned in Season 6, Veronica was added in the show's opening making it look like she'll be a major character. But aside her return episode, Veronica doesn't have any major episodes and just shows up. Alpha Bitch: Has the personality of a ditzy and spoiled party girl despite being an adult,she gets better though. Brainless Beauty: Got through school by using her looks and teasing. Doesn't work out as well when she becomes an adult as she is expected to do more than tease. Cloudcuckoolander: Briefly when she gets stoned in her debut episode. Contrasting Sequel Main Character: To her cousin Carmen. Unlike Carmen who is middle class and is regarded as a smart student, Veronica is very rich but not very smart.

characters.name: Mr. Needles
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He vanishes after season 3. Considering his numerous health problems, there's a good chance he simply died off-screen. Meaningful Name: As Max explains, "Mr. Needles" is called such due to the injections he's regularly given.

characters.name: Linda Lorenzo
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Her adoptive parents were Italian and she definitely looked the part. Though she does mention that she's often "mistaken" for being Latina. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She only appeared in three episodes and was mentioned once in passing afterwards when George met Benny's mother. Though considering what happened in her final appearance, her departure was probably justified. Daddy Had a Good Reason for Abandoning You: A mother example. The reason she was given away is because Benny was unable to afford taking care of a second child after Manny left. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: Responsible to George's foolish. She's a college graduate and a superintendent of Max's school district. Happily Adopted: She never knew she was adopted until George told her and she was crushed when the news broke. Though she eventually comes to accept her biological family (mostly George).

characters.name: Manny Lopez
characters.description: Daddy Had a Good Reason for Abandoning You: Tries to invoke this by claiming that he left because he could no longer get along with Benny and believed that both of them would be better off without him, when in reality, he was just fed up with Benny and left so he could start over. Death Equals Redemption: Harshly averted.He leaves George with a memento in the form of a watch...but asks him and Benny to not attend his funeral in order to preserve his reputation to those he actually considered family and friends. Any improvement in the relationship he had with his son and ex-wife is immediately thrown out the window, and George and Benny likely will never forgive him. Doting Parent: He spoiled his second son, before finally cutting him off for good after being fed up with his irresponsibility. Dirty Coward: Instead of trying to deal with his marital problems with Benny, or openly tell her the marriage wasn't working out, he basically ran away from her.He was this even from beyond the grave, telling George not to go his funeral because he didn't want people to know he abandoned his family. Disappeared Dad: Obviously.

characters.name: JasonMcNamara
characters.description: The Ace:George:Are you sure you can be here? The super popular kids might see you! You could lose your reputation! And have to eat lunch with...the debate team!Jason:I'm captain of the debate team. All Take and No Give: He's the taker in his relationship with Carmen, who supports his dreams, forgives his mess ups, and convinced her parents to take him in. For Jason himself, Jason hardly put in the effort - when they began their romance; he was embarrassed to be seen with her; he became angry and moody towards her after taking steroids; he then cheated on her despite all of the acts she did; and when she did forgive him for his infidelity, he gets cold feet in their marriage and cowardly abandoned her to go to school instead of properly discussing their different mindsets. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Zigzagged. Jason does have some genuine moments of being kind, but he often does horrible acts while trying to still be seen as a nice person. Broken Ace: Jason is aHunkyChick Magnet, talented football player, and even gets straight A's. And while he came off as a straight example ofThe Ace, he turns out to be this trope. He comes from a neglectful home life, he took steroids at one point to please his father and is far from a supportive boyfriend to Carmen, being emotionally negligent at best and emotionally abusive at worst. Chick Magnet: Besides Carmen, many girls swoon over him.

characters.name: Emilina Palmero
characters.description: Alas, Poor Villain: Despite being aJerkasswho cheated on her husband who's also the father of her children, her untimely death is played quite somberly, as both Angie and Vic break down in tears after hearing the unfortunate news. Angie alsofeels terrible for calling her a selfish tramp in their last conversation. Doting Grandparent: According to Veronica, she was an adoring grandma who helped her through rehab, bailed her out after she shoplifted, and even let her get away withcrashing Emilina's car. Jerkass: Her sole onscreen appearance revolved around her treating George like crap. She also cheated on her husband for no real reason. George even calls her "one bitter tramp with a 10-foot stick up her butt." Jerk with a Heart of Gold: While the above is true, Emilina did love her daughter and she was in the midst of reconciling with her ex-husband before her death. Veronica even says Emilina was aDoting Grandparentwho did a lot for her. Heel–Face Door-Slam: Vic and Emilina were in the process of reconciliation before her death. She also died before she and her daughter Angie could repair their relationship.

characters.name: Jack and Mel Powers
characters.description: Dirty Old Man: Mel when Veronica flirts with him to make George's life miserable. George convinces him he made them reservations at a nice hotel and Mel went off to get "magic pills". Kick the Dog: Mel slept with Jack's wife while they were still married. He even gloats about it:Jack:You know when I look at you, Mel, I don't see a brother. I see a worthless, backstabbingJUDAS!Mel:Oh yeah? What do you see now?[makes orgasmic facial expressions]Well, you wouldn't recognize that, would you? Because that's the face Janet makes when she's beensatisfied! Mean Boss:George:We need a new dental plan. It'll cost a little more, but the workers deserve it.Powers:All I heard was, "Cost a little more," then a bunch of whistles and sirens. Parental Neglect: Mel is a deadbeat dad who more or less enables Zack'ssociopathicbehavior. In Zack's second appearance, it's even said that Mel missed his 17th birthday party just yesterday. Also in "George to the Third Power", Mel admits to getting high on painkillers so he doesn't have to listen to Zack's complaining. Reasonable Authority Figure: Despite being corruptjerkasses, as stated above, they sincerely respect George and are always willing to listen to his ideas even if they won't agree with them and are sincerely apologetic whenever he tells them that they've offended him in some way. They've even helped him with some family problems, such as planning his vow renewal, ordering Zack to tell the truth about what happened to Carmen, and teaching Max not to lie and the value of hard work. Of course, that doesn't mean they forgive George for going behind their backs and made it a point to tell his family exactly what his punishment was.

characters.name: Gina Sorenstam
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To George. Ambiguously Bi: "You don't need a man to have sex." Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Averted. Interestingly, she's actually the only character you'd expect to fall victim who doesn't. Dirty Old Woman: Even more so than Benny. Small Name, Big Ego: Very clearly sees herself as more enticing andsexually appealingthan she is.

characters.name: "Accident" Amy Kirkland
characters.description: Generation Xerox: In one episode, she has a daughter who is just as accident prone as she is. The Klutz: She's very clumsy, hence why peopl call her "Accident Amy". Phrase Catcher: When Ernie sees her, he always exclaims "Accident Amy! Breaking bones and breaking hearts." Plucky Comic Relief: Primarily acts as this up until her last appearance. Put on a Bus: After her last appearance, Amy suddenly left the show.

characters.name: Zack Powers
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Towards Carmen. He spoils her with gifts and compliments so she'll like him, but it's clearly just an act so she'll sleep with him. Towards everyone else though, he's just a straight-upJerkass. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: To Piper Morey. Both are snotty, two-faced teens who go out of their way to hurt Carmen, and are the reason she's forced to leave high schooltwice.Despite Piper's bullying, however, she wasn't necessarily a criminal, unlike Zack who has committed theft, assault (includingsexualassault), reproductive abuse, underage drinking, vandalism, embezzlement, and drug distribution. Furthermore, Zack regularly gets away with his actions due to being the son of an aerospace factory owner, while Piper doesn't even last a day without getting suspended from school despite being the class president. Both of them also get violently beaten by a female Lopez. Daddy Issues: He vandalized his dad's factory out of complete spite. Mel thinks it was Benny at first, but later discovers it was Zack because he wrote "I hate you, Daddy" in graffiti in the psychologist's office. Date Rape: Attempted in the Season 4 premiere. He plans to take her to a hotel so they can down a bottle of vodka together, promising to "take care of [her]" if she gets too dizzy from the alcohol. It's pretty clear to the audience that Zack's intentions are far from innocent, since he literally told George last episode that he was gonna dump her after they had sex. Thankfully, Carmen sees what he's trying to do and dumpshimfirst. Deadpan Snarker: While calling Carmen on the phone at work, Zack gives George a mocking thumbs-up while telling who the latter thinks is a sheet metal supplier that he's seen and likes their "product". He also gives George a snarky goodbye after getting fired from the factory.

characters.name: RandyMcGee
characters.description: The Big Guy: Very big and loud, towering over Benny. Double Standard: Rape, Female on Male: George catches Accident Amy forcing a make out session on Randy which he clearly wasn't consenting to, but is upset withhimfor not pulling away and takes it as evidence of him not really being over Amy. When George tells Angie what he saw, both of them are completely focused on the kiss and not, you know, how a future member of their family wassexually assaulted. Nice Guy: Despite leaving Benny at the altar, he's one of the friendlier characters on the show. Satellite Love Interest: Doesn't have much character aside from being Benny's lover. What the Hell, Hero?: Accident Amy tells Randy at his bachelor party that she's willing to give him what Benny can't: kids. While Randy doesn't outright dump Benny, he says he has some things to think about, which Benny rips into him for.

characters.name: George Edward Lopez II
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He stopped appearing afterManny's Deathand was never mentioned again. Everyone Has Standards: While he has no problem using a sob story to get money from his half-brother, he gets defensive when George accuses him of identity fraud. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: Foolish to George I's responsible. A college dropout who blew through his trust fund and was drowning in debt. His job at a skate shop apparently doesn't pay much. My Greatest Failure: He regretfully admits to taking advantage of Manny to act like a spoiled jerk. Nice Guy: He did break a trust fund with his dad when he was younger and did try to get $500 from George but almost everything else he does shows he does seem to be a rather friendly and caring guy. He was even willing togive a kidney to Manny until it turned out that they weren't compatible.

characters.name: Luisa Diaz
characters.description: Abusive Parents: She admits to spanking Benny "sometimes in the face". She also called Benny a whore and tells her that she's worthless. In a courtroom no less. Distinction Without a Difference: When Benny calls her out for the times she hit her during her sentencing hearing, Luisa insists that they "spanked her, sometimes in the face." Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Subverted. She does rush to the Lopez house when George lies that she's been shot, but later events show that she truly doesn't have any real love for her daughter. Hate Sink: Luisa is a portrayal of abusive mothers that isn'tPlayed for Laughs. While Benny has moments of humor and sympathy, Luisa is just a walking ball of hate with no redeeming qualities. Seriously, after she cruelly insults Benny while testifying during the sentencing hearing, you will want tostrangleher. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: When we first meet Luisa, she seems like a stern but reasonable woman who has some understandable reasons to be annoyed with Benny but is willing to put it aside to keep her out of prison. Then she's put on the stand, and we see how heartless she really is. While she did seem truly concerned when George lured her over by telling her that Benny had been shot, she likely would have just been there to gloat if that were true, judging by her parting comments at the end of the episode.

characters.name: Lou Powers
characters.description: The Alcoholic: Lou's primary characteristic is being a heavy drinker. Benevolent Boss: Implied by Benny that he deeply cared about his workers when he was around. Since it's Benny of all people saying it, he must have been a saint. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Particularly glaring in theGrand Finale, when Jack tries to sell the business and Lou's share in the company isn't brought up at all. Hidden Depths: A financial genius, according to Benny. Real Life Writes the Plot: Only appeared in one episode and was never seen or mentioned again, due to the passing of Paul Gleason in 2006.

characters.name: Marisol
characters.description: Domestic Abuse: Her boyfriend, Junior, is shown to be physically and verbally abusive. Sour Outside, Sad Inside: As George explained to Carmen why she shouldn't look up to Marisol, her toughness is an act. Deep down she's scared and unsure what to do with her life. What Happened to the Mouse?: It's never explained what happened to her after helping out with Benny's cleaning.

characters.name: Piper Morey
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: She is a snobby bitch. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: In her first appearance, Piper sends an anonymous email fat-shaming Toby, Carmen's best friend since kindergarten. She also plans to invite Toby to a party just to bully hermore. Hate Sink: There isnothinggood or likable about Piper. The only vaguely nice thing Piper does for Carmen is buy her a pillow...and even then, it is just an excuse to call her a slut. Jerkass: Bullies Carmen out of school, all for not joining in on insulting a friend. Laser-Guided Karma: Piper gets suspended from school when George and Angie prove that she was the one who instigated the fight with Carmen.

characters.name: Ricky
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: Once Ernie adopts him, he's only seen two more times and is then only mentioned from time to time. Freudian Excuse: His dad ran out on him and his mom is a rough alcoholic and horrible person. It is not known if she became who she is because of her husband leaving. Happily Adopted: By Ernie. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He started off as a bad influence on Max for a bit. Despite that, he actually really does care about Max and does value his friendship with him. Mirror Character: To George. Just like him, his father abandoned him and his mother is a neglectful, washed up drunk. When George learns this, he decides toforgive him for driving the car through a fence.

characters.name: Tammy
characters.description: The Alcoholic: She's even worse than Benny. Foil: To Angie. While Angie is a good mother who does genuinely care for George, Tammy clearly abuses Ernie for his money, openly cheats on him and is extremely neglectful towards Ricky. Hate Sink: Tammy is a selfish, neglectful mother who takes advantage of Ernie's kindness and mooches off his money, all the while she's cheating on him with other men and even briefly manipulates him into thinking he's the father of her unborn child. Put on a Bus: Ernie casually mentions that he figured out Tammy was cheating on him with other men while he was at work, so the relationship ended permanently. Took a Level in Jerkass: In her first appearance, her situation was portrayed sympathetically, as she lamented Ricky's deadbeat dad deserting her and how hard it is to raise a kid while struggling with drinking. In her second appearance, she's on the wagon, but she's also actively treating Ernie badly and taking advantage of him.

characters.name: Eddie Carter
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's an armed robber, but he's also a genuineNice Guytowards George and Max when they talk in the convenience store, and he really dotes on Benny for the most part until selling her out to the cops while thinking she turned him in. Eddie was an especially good friend towards George during the latter's childhood, always taking him to dodger games and even buying him his first beer at 14...George:...innings into a great game on my 21st birthday. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Gender-Inverted. He tells George that he'll never find another woman like Benny, which actually shocks the former and makes him question if he's on medication. Even Evil Has Standards: According to Benny, Eddie has "shot fewer people thanthe vice president", implying he draws the line at murder despite being an armed robber. Evil Is Petty: He almost immediately turns on Benny and gives her up to the cops when he believes she turned him in to the police. Fat Bastard: He's overweight and an armed robber.

characters.name: Ray Palmero
characters.description: Black Sheep: He's easily the worst member of the Palmero family, being a criminal and all. Angie and Vic have much contempt for him. Con Man: He's a con artist who talks and/or just robs relatives, elderly, children, whole families, and finallyhis own daughterout of their money. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Zigzagged: He stole from Veronica in the past, and tried to do it again. However, he does claim to still care about Veronica and only robbed her because he owes money to a lot of dangerous people. And he did pay Victor back...albeit by pulling another con. While George throws Ray out of Veronica's life, he tells Veronica that what Ray did wasn't out of malice, but desperation. Freudian Excuse: While stealing from his daughter is wrong on so many levels, Ray admits he's in deep with some very unsavory figures, and Vic admits he ruined Ray by spoiling him rotten. Hate Sink: He's a selfish, manipulative con artist who will gladly throw his own family members, including his owndaughterunder the bus to get some extra cash. It's clear that Ray isn't meant to be liked.

characters.name: Cris Watson
characters.description: The Atoner: Despite committing ahorriblecrime five years ago, Watson at least admits that what she did was wrong, is still going to therapy, and has turned her life around so that she can afford to live in a middle-class neighborhood. She even rejects Max's advances when he comes to her house. Double Standard: Rape, Female on Male:Deconstructed. Watson had sex with a male minor in the past, because of which George gathers an angry mob of neighbors to harass her at her house, but when the sex offender in question turns out to be a hot woman, everyone leaves, with George even saying that it's all good and the boy must've been lucky; Angie is the only person here who (rightfully) finds thecompletedouble standard disturbing. But later on when Max goes to Watson's house with a condom to lose his virginity to her, George finally realizes howwrong and stupidhe was because his own child could've been scarred for life at worst, and gottensomeone genuinely trying to turn her life aroundrearrested at best. Hot Teacher: She's a former high school teacher, and George himself calls her hot.Downplayed, however, in that she still abused her teaching jobandgood looks to victimize a 15-year-old boy in the past. Mirror Character: To Zack Powers. Both got kicked out of high school for sexual offenses; Zack was a student who got the principal's daughter pregnant (implicitly on purpose), and Cris was a teacher who raped a male undergraduate. However, while Zack wasThe Sociopathwho used his rich father's connections to get away with his delinquency, Cris isThe Atonerwho served actual prison time and has been attending therapy since her release. Despite said past offenses, Carmen and Max respectively try to lose their virginities to them, but unlike Cris with the latter, Zack went out of his way trying to screw up the former's life by seducing her into becoming a runaway. And, unlike with Cris, George pretty much hated Zack at first sight. Wouldn't Hurt a Child: Despite molesting a child i

characters.name: Hector Vega
characters.description: Anti-Villain: While the antagonist of the final episode, he doesn't seem to be a bad person overall and is moved to help George and the current workers out of genuine altruism. While by that point he had already learned about a tax credit he'd get from keeping them onboard, he is moved by George's loyalty to his people nonetheless. Final Boss: He is the main antagonist of the final episode of the series, and on a thematic level he tests George's loyalty to all his friends and family he's made over the course of the series and at the factory. George standing his ground against him results ina happy ending for everyone. Not So Above It All: While a straight-laced businessman, when George yells at him that he will accept his offer, but asks him to yell too to make it look like he's standing his ground, Vega is amused and does so to help him save face. Pragmatic Villainy: Aside from agreeing to do it out of the decency of his heart, he learns that he gets a substantial tax credit if he keeps all the original owners for the factory. Reasonable Authority Figure: When he sees how many people will be affected by the closure, he is genuinely moved and works out a solution to help them and George.
